messages:
alisa ng: quick heads-up — brought up a quantized 13B (mix q4_k + int8-dyn fallback) with an early-prefetch speculative path (prototype flag = --spec-early-prefix). first smoke: latency down ~18% p50, tokens/sec +22%. quality checks: NQ-open EM dropped ~1.2 pts vs fp16 baseline.

matt k: can you paste the exact eval command and the perf numbers? also, which dataset split?

alisa ng: ran: `./run_eval.sh --model ./weights/13b-qmix --spec-mode early --batch 8 --seq 1024 --evalsets nq-open,hot100`
perf summary (local devbox, A100s): p50=53ms (was 65ms), p95=210ms (was 230ms), tokens/sec=680 (was 560). eval EM: baseline fp16=84.7, current quant+spec=83.5.

ryan p: interesting. 1.2 EM is small but suspicious. did you enable the early-prefetch score-correction? iirc we had a bug where prefix cache reuse skipped renormalization for top-k sampling.

alisa ng: i used the default sampler from the proto: `topk=40, temp=0.8, speculative_prefetch=true` — not score-correction. good call.

sophie t: short checklist: 1) rerun with deterministic greedy to isolate sampling noise, 2) rerun with spec-prefetch off (only qmix quant), 3) run perplexity on heldout to see if probability mass shifted.

matt k: agree. also run paired bootstrap or simple paired t-test over the same prompts to get significance. 1.2 might be within noise.

alisa ng: doing quick ablation now. first result: greedy (no sampling) -> fp16 EM 86.1 vs quant+spec greedy 85.9 (delta 0.2). quant-only (spec off) with sampling -> EM 84.9 (delta 0.2 vs baseline sampling). so looks like majority of the drop happens only when spec+sampling combine.

ryan p: that points to interaction between speculative beam candidates and sampling temperature/topk. speculation can bias logits if prefetch candidates are rescored incorrectly under sampling. can you dump logits for a few failed examples?

alisa ng: uploading 3 examples to /tmp/spec-debug-dumps (attached below). example format: `{"prompt_id": 123, "prefix": "...", "baseline_top5": [...], "spec_top5": [...], "baseline_probs": [...], "spec_probs": [...]}`

ops-bot: deploy-logs: new-spec-flag rolled to devpool at 7372818065 — 4 pods.

matt k: nice. alisa, when you dump logits, include the prefetch candidate tokens and the final chosen token distribution after rescore. we need to check normalization and whether temperature was applied twice.

alisa ng: log sample for prompt 123: baseline_probs [0.42,0.18,0.06,...], spec_probs [0.52,0.10,0.03,...] — spec overconfident on top token. appears we forgot to re-normalize after merging KV-prefetch and live-step logits under tempered sampling.

sophie t: if spec is boosting the top candidate, that can increase average token confidence but harm sampling diversity -> lower EM on tasks that need precise answers. fix is likely: apply inverse-temp correction on prefetched logits before merge or compute candidate weights under sampling distribution.

ryan p: another quick mitigator: clamp prefetch logits with a simple bias cap: logit' = min(logit, logit_top + delta) before softmax. test with delta=2.0.

alisa ng: ran clamp test: delta=2.0 -> sampling EM back to 84.6 (vs 84.7 baseline). latency impact negligible. tokens/sec -0.5%. promising.

matt k: OK this is actionable. let's: 1) add temp-correction + clamp default in spec runtime; 2) add unit test that compares rescore distribution vs baseline under multiple temps; 3) rerun full eval (NQ, RACE, Hot100) and post numbers to this thread.

sophie t: also log a followup to ops: add a rollout guard that disables spec-prefetch for any model flagged as "new-quant" until we pass quality gates. safer for canaries.

ops-bot: rollout-note created: RB-1493 (spec-prefetch guard) by sophie.t at 7372818105.

alisa ng: thanks — I'll push a small PR with the clamp + temp-correction and attach new evals once CI finishes. attaching quick perf diff: p50 unchanged, p95 +3ms due to extra normalization, tokens/sec -1.5%.

matt k: sounds good. if CI shows regressions anywhere else, we can default the guard to off. great work team. :thumbsup:

alisa ng: PR link: https://git.redwood/inference/pull/3125 — includes tests and toggles. will post final evals in ~30m.

ryan p: if final evals look clean, schedule a small canary with the guard off for dedicated nodes so customers see the perf win but quality is protected.

sophie t: noted. tagging @eng-sre for canary ops planning.

matt k: thanks. short takeaway: speculative prefetch can give real latency gains, but under sampling we must ensure correct rescore normalization; small fixes recover quality while preserving most perf.

alisa ng: final evals (CI finished): NQ-open sampling EM: baseline 84.7 -> patched spec 84.6 (delta -0.1), RACE acc: baseline 77.2 -> patched 77.1, Hot100 F1: baseline 68.9 -> patched 68.7. all within noise.

ops-bot: CI status: all checks passed at 7372818118.

matt k: perfect. merge when you're ready.

alisa ng: merging now. thanks all. :rocket:
